🦀 ELI5 Kata · Sum of Four Squares (Rust, 1 kyu)

Lagrange proved every number N = a² + b² + c² + d².
How do we decompose huge 1024-bit numbers in ~0.25 ms each in pure Rust without GMP?

https://github.com/8b-is/space-bender/tree/main/katas/1kyu/express-number-as-sum-of-four-squares

🪆 ELI5 Step 1 (The Double-Sqrt Cascade):

Instead of testing 1024-bit primes:
1. Pick `a ≈ √n` (512 bits) → remainder `r1 = n - a²` shrinks to ~513 bits!
2. Pick `b ≈ √r1` (257 bits) → remainder `p = r1 - b²` shrinks to ~258 bits (`[u64; 5]`)!

⚡ ELI5 Step 2 (Parity Lock + Stack Montgomery):

Matching `(a, b)` parities to `n mod 4` forces `p = n - a² - b² ≡ 1 (mod 4)` every time!
96 small primes filter 85% of steps in `u32`, and stack `[u64; 5]` Montgomery Miller-Rabin + Cornacchia finds `c² + d² = p` with 0 heap allocs!

✅ All 20×2^128 + 20×2^1024 random tests solved in ~7.2 ms total in Rust!
